findings.title: SQL Injection
findings.rationale: Scanner confidence is Low, the target is a static CSS file with a cache-busting parameter, evidence is empty, and the only signal is a 3-byte response-length difference. A static asset does not query a database.
findings.remediation: Confirm with a manual retest (sqlmap or a parameterized request) against the static asset; if not reproducible, document as a false positive with the retest output attached.
findings.ticket_summary: Probable false positive: boolean SQLi flagged on static CSS query param 'v'; requires manual retest before POA&M entry.

findings.title: Cross Site Scripting (Reflected)
findings.rationale: The injected script payload is reflected verbatim in the response on two endpoints (/search param q, /help param topic), which is direct evidence of unencoded output.
findings.remediation: Apply context-aware output encoding in the search and help templates, add server-side allow-list validation for q and topic, and add a Content-Security-Policy that blocks inline script.
findings.ticket_summary: Reflected XSS on /search (q) and /help (topic); payload echoed unencoded. Fix via output encoding + input validation.

findings.title: Content Security Policy (CSP) Header Not Set
findings.rationale: The CSP header is absent across 14 responses; this is a configuration baseline gap that also increases XSS impact.
findings.remediation: Add a Content-Security-Policy header at the nginx layer starting with default-src 'self' in report-only mode, then enforce after one week of reports.
findings.ticket_summary: CSP header missing on 14 responses; add baseline CSP at nginx.

findings.title: Missing Anti-clickjacking Header
findings.rationale: The login page does not set X-Frame-Options or a frame-ancestors directive, so it can be framed by another origin.
findings.remediation: Set Content-Security-Policy frame-ancestors 'none' (or X-Frame-Options DENY) on all authenticated and login pages.

findings.title: Vulnerable JS Library
findings.rationale: The served file banner identifies jQuery 1.12.4, which the scanner flags as a vulnerable library version.
findings.remediation: Upgrade jQuery to the current supported release, run the UI regression suite, and add dependency scanning to CI so outdated libraries fail the build.
findings.ticket_summary: Outdated jQuery 1.12.4 served from /static/js; upgrade and add CI dependency scan.

findings.title: Cookie Without Secure Flag
findings.rationale: The session_id cookie set on POST /login lacks the Secure flag, so it could be sent over an unencrypted channel.
findings.remediation: Set Secure, HttpOnly and SameSite=Strict on session_id in the auth middleware and verify with a response-header test.
findings.ticket_summary: session_id cookie missing Secure flag on /login.

findings.title: Server Leaks Version Information via "Server" HTTP Response Header Field
findings.rationale: The Server header exposes the exact nginx version on 20 responses, helping attackers fingerprint known weaknesses.
findings.remediation: Set server_tokens off in nginx.conf and redeploy; confirm the header no longer contains a version string.
findings.ticket_summary: nginx version exposed in Server header; set server_tokens off.

findings.title: Information Disclosure - Suspicious Comments
findings.rationale: A TODO comment was found in app.js; this is informational and usually harmless, but comments should be stripped from production bundles.
findings.remediation: Enable comment stripping in the production JavaScript build step and rebuild the bundle.
findings.ticket_summary: Informational: TODO comments in app.js bundle; strip in build.

executive_summary: Fix the reflected XSS on /search and /help first; it is the only confirmed High with direct evidence and a 30-day FedRAMP window. The High SQL injection is very likely a false positive on a static CSS file and needs a manual retest before any POA&M entry. The Moderate header and jQuery findings can ship together in one hardening change. Low findings are quick nginx and cookie configuration fixes.
